title: Technical Architect
description:
Role Overview Architect and build a scalable, event-driven, AI-enabled full-stack platform with strong ownership across backend, frontend, and system design. Drive systems that are observable, resilient, secure, and production-grade by design, not as afterthoughts. Core Responsibilities 1. Design Event-Driven Systems Build systems using event-first architecture (NATS or similar), not REST-centric design. Define event contracts, schemas, naming conventions, and lifecycle flows. Ensure idempotency for safe reprocessing. Implement retry strategies, including exponential backoff and Dead Letter Queues (DLQs). Ensure failure isolation, recovery, and loose coupling between services. Implement event versioning and backward compatibility strategies. 2. Build Scalable Backend (Spring Boot) Develop domain-driven microservices with clear bounded contexts. Use REST APIs for synchronous UI interactions and events for asynchronous workflows and orchestration. Ensure high throughput, low latency, and secure service-to-service communication. Apply clean architecture principles, including layered or hexagonal architecture where applicable. Implement caching, connection pooling, and performance tuning. 3. Integrate AI Agents (Python Services) Treat AI as a decoupled, event-driven service layer. Design asynchronous execution through events. Implement timeouts, retries, and circuit breakers. Develop fallback strategies for degraded AI responses. Handle non-deterministic AI outputs safely. Work with OpenAI, Anthropic, and Amazon Bedrock. Implement prompt versioning, traceability, and response auditing. 4. Build Modern Frontend (Angular) Develop responsive Single Page Applications (SPAs) using Angular. Visualize real-time workflow execution and system state. Implement efficient state management and reactive programming using RxJS. Optimize performance through lazy loading and appropriate change detection strategies. Integrate event streams and WebSockets for live updates. 5. Identity & Security (SSO) Implement and integrate SAML, OAuth 2.0/OIDC, and CAS. Ensure secure token propagation across services. Implement role-based access control (RBAC) and attribute-based access control (ABAC). Ensure secure secrets management. Address zero-trust architecture and service authentication patterns. 6. Data & System Design Use PostgreSQL or similar RDBMS technologies with strong schema design discipline. Avoid tight coupling across services and shared database anti-patterns. Ensure data consistency, including eventual consistency where required. Maintain auditability and traceability. Design systems for multi-tenancy, high availability, data partitioning, and scalability. 7. Observability & Reliability Build first-class observability into every component. Implement structured logging with correlation IDs and trace IDs. Monitor metrics such as latency, throughput, error rates, and queue depth. Implement distributed tracing using OpenTelemetry or similar tools. Define and monitor SLIs, SLOs, and SLAs. Implement health checks and readiness probes. Configure alerting and dashboards using Prometheus, Grafana, or similar tools. Enable end-to-end traceability across event-driven workflows and AI calls. 8. DevOps & Platform Engineering Work in Linux environments with strong command-line proficiency. Use Git, Maven, and CI/CD pipelines. Build continuously deployable systems using Infrastructure as Code (IaC), including Terraform or CloudFormation. Ensure environment parity across development, staging, and production. Implement rollback strategies and safe deployment practices. Non-Functional Requirements (Explicit Ownership) The candidate will be responsible for designing systems that meet the following requirements: Scalability: Horizontal scaling and event throughput handling. Reliability: Fault tolerance and graceful degradation. Performance: Low-latency APIs and efficient asynchronous processing. Security: End-to-end secure architecture. Observability: Full system visibility and traceability. Maintainability: Clean code and modular design. Extensibility: Plug-and-play connectors and workflows. Cost Efficiency: Optimized infrastructure and compute usage. Compliance Readiness: Audit logs and access tracking. Required Skills Must-Have Skills 10+ years of experience in enterprise application development. Strong expertise in Java and Spring Boot. Strong experience with event-driven architecture using NATS, Kafka, or similar technologies. Strong Angular expertise, with at least 3+ years of SPA development experience. Experience with microservices architecture. Strong knowledge of SQL and Hibernate. Experience in distributed systems design. Good-to-Have Skills AI/LLM integration experience. IAM and SSO systems, including SAML, OAuth 2.0, and CAS. Cloud platforms, preferably AWS. Workflow and orchestration systems. Experience with observability stacks such as OpenTelemetry, Prometheus, and Grafana.

Key Skills: Java,Spring Boot,Technical Architecture,Angular,Microservices,AWS,Spring,Boot

Strong familiarity with cloud platforms such as AWS, Azure, or GCP , and practical knowledge of AI/ML services like SageMaker , Vertex AI , or Azure ML . Architectural experience with vector databases (e.g., Pinecone, FAISS, Weaviate, Qdrant ) for semantic search and RAG pipelines. Understanding of DevOps practices , including Docker , Kubernetes , and infrastructure as code. Knowledge of CI/CD processes , system security , and observability/monitoring frameworks . GenAI & AI/ML Architecture Knowledge: Sound understanding of GenAI system components , including LLM lifecycles , embedding generation , prompt orchestration , and RAG architectures . Ability to architect complete GenAI workflows , from context ingestion and enrichment to inference handling and post-processing. Familiarity with API orchestration , agent-based design patterns , and semantic search strategies. While direct data science work is not required, a strong grasp of AI/ML engineering principles and pipeline design is expected to ensure architecture aligns with model and data needs.
